title: Seeking Fairness at Work: Cracking the New Code of Greater Employee Engagement, Retention & Satisfaction
author: Laraine Kaminsky
target_audience: Consultants and coaches in workplace culture
core_themes: Defining fairness in the modern workplace
Employee engagement and retention as outcomes of fair practices
The relationship between perceived fairness, satisfaction, and productivity
Inclusive leadership and equitable management practices
Addressing unconscious bias and systemic inequity
Building trust and transparency in organizations
primary_purpose: To provide leaders, HR professionals, and organizations with actionable insights and frameworks for cultivating fairness in the workplace, thereby driving higher employee engagement, improving retention, and boosting overall satisfaction and organizational performance.

structure_format.narrative_style: Practical, research-backed, and conversational with real-world case studies
structure_format.organization: Structured around key pillars of fairness (such as transparency, equity, inclusion, and voice), with actionable steps and reflective questions at the end of each section
features: Personal stories and case studies from diverse workplaces
Reflection and action prompts for readers

key_concepts_lessons: Fairness is a multi-dimensional concept that includes transparency, equity, consistency, and inclusion.
Employee perceptions of fairness significantly affect engagement, retention, and job satisfaction.
Addressing biases and reviewing organizational systems is essential for lasting change.
Open communication, listening to diverse voices, and involving employees in decision-making fosters fairness.
Fairness is not a one-time initiative but an ongoing commitment requiring regular measurement and adjustment.
Managers and leaders have a pivotal role in modeling and championing fair practices.
notable_features: Fresh research on the 'fairness gap' in today's organizations
Action-oriented frameworks for leaders and HR professionals
Exploration of modern fairness challenges including hybrid/remote work dynamics and generational expectations
Toolkit for organizations to self-assess fairness and track progress
cultural_historical_context: Written in the wake of major shifts in the workplace post-pandemic, heightened expectations for employee voice, and renewed attention to DEI, the book responds to urgent organizational challenges around trust, talent retention, and fairness in a changing world of work.
reception_impact: Positively received by HR and leadership communities for bridging research and actionable steps
Highlighted in DEI and management circles for its practical assessment frameworks
Used in leadership development and HR training programs
Appreciated for case studies and its human-centered, inclusive approach to workplace change
comparable_titles: Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us by Daniel H. Pink
Inclusion on Purpose by Ruchika Tulshyan
The Fearless Organization by Amy C. Edmondson
How to Be an Inclusive Leader by Jennifer Brown
